column1: # Campaign 24 test evidence for exact clustered signed BIGINT range detachment.

column8: note

Eight focused tests cover the exact non-null signed clustered-handle comparison subset, conjunctions, residual partition, and boundary normalization; the original typed SQL-expression matrix remains open.
Signed MIN and MAX strict and non-strict boundaries are overflow-safe; unsigned and index ranges remain open.
Six comparison operators and ordered AND intersection are covered for one signed clustered column; general column types and SQL expressions remain open.
Only the common signed-integer boundary behavior is covered; YEAR conversion and index behavior remain open.
Closed signed handle intervals are normalized; prefix indexes and string truncation remain open.
Exact integer comparison and intersection behavior is covered; multidatum indexes, IN, DNF, NULL, coercion, and collations remain open.
Only the underlying signed table-handle interval semantics are covered; shard indexes remain open.
Only the underlying signed table-handle interval semantics are covered; shard expression suites remain open.
Access indices and residuals are returned without aliasing, but range memory quota fallback and index detachment remain open.
Exact bounded table ranges are covered with no fallback; range memory quota fallback remains open.
Exact bounded table-handle ranges are covered; general column ranges and memory fallback remain open.
Normalized nonoverlapping integer ranges are covered; prefix-index behavior remains open.
The bounded signed comparison subset remains panic-free at extreme values; the issue-specific expression shape remains open.

Ordered CNF access indices are exact; DNF and minimum-access-condition selection remain open.
Binary signed integers need no collation; string collation and index behavior remain open.
Inclusive signed range construction and endpoints are covered; multidatum, exclusion flags, encoding, and formatting remain open.
The exact full signed handle interval is covered; unsigned, NULL, and multidatum full-range recognition remain open.
The bounded value type allocates no per-range heap state; Go memory accounting remains open.
Ordered list intersection is covered for signed inclusive ranges; general multidatum range lists remain open.
Contradictory comparisons produce an empty range list; general empty intersection cases remain open.
Redundant bounds preserve the narrower signed range; general subset APIs remain open.
Overlapping and split not-equal ranges intersect without overlap; multidatum overlap behavior remains open.
